name: binhex-caddy-duckdns
description: Caddy is a powerful, enterprise-ready, open source web server with automatic HTTPS written in Go. This image includes the DuckDNS DNS challenge plugin, enabling automatic TLS certificate issuance and renewal via Let's Encrypt for DuckDNS hostnames without requiring port 80 to be open. Ideal for use as a reverse proxy on a home network.

paths.name: Path: /config
paths.description: This is the container path to your Caddy configuration file (Caddyfile) and logs.

ports.name: Port: HTTPS
ports.description: The HTTPS port Caddy listens on. Must match https_port in your Caddyfile.

ports.name: Port: HTTP
ports.description: The HTTP port Caddy listens on (used for redirects). Must match http_port in your Caddyfile.

ports.name: Port: Admin
ports.description: The admin edpoint port for Caddy.

variables.name: Variable: DUCKDNS_TOKEN
variables.description: Duck DNS token for automatic TLS certificate issuance and renewal, sign into Duck DNS to view your token.

variables.name: Variable: HEALTHCHECK_COMMAND
variables.description: The command or script to execute, if not specified then the script healthcheck.sh will be used (process, dns and https checking).

variables.name: Variable: HEALTHCHECK_ACTION
variables.description: The action to execute if the healthcheck command returns a non zero exit code, if not specified the action will be 'exit 1', if you want the container to exit on failure then set the action to 'kill 1'.

variables.name: Variable: HEALTHCHECK_HOSTNAME
variables.description: The hostname used when performing HTTPS and DNS healthchecking.

variables.name: Variable: PUID
variables.description: User ID for the running container

variables.name: Variable: PGID
variables.description: Group ID for the running container
